text:
alex: Heads-up: apne2 queue depth creeping fast for mistral-7b-instruct and redwood-embed-1. Seen sustained backlog growth over last 8m.

alex: Metrics snapshot: queue_depth_total=2124 (+1.8k in 10m), active_gpu_pods=42/48, avg_wait_ms=1420, tail_99p_latency=3.9s.

jamie: ack. Any heavy customers in that region?

alex: Two big tenants: [acme-commerce] and an internal evaluation job from growth-team running long-context evals. Per-model split: mistral-7b-instruct ~66% of queued requests, redwood-embed-1 ~22%, misc small models remainder.

tiago: Can we confirm admission-control thresholds? last change was yesterday evening for apne2.

sasha: pull of current admission policy:
```json
{ "region": "apne2", "max_inflight_per_model": 80, "global_queue_limit": 2000, "priority_weights": {"enterprise": 1.2, "self-serve": 0.8}}
```

kai: global_queue_limit is 2000 so we're right at the edge. queue_depth_total 2124 means some requests are getting queued but not yet evicted. Looks like burst came from growth eval.

alex: I'm going to flip a soft throttle for self-serve in apne2 to protect enterprise traffic. will push a conservative 20% cap on new self-serve tokens for next 15m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

deploy-bot: admission-control update applied (id=ac-20240301-171986). region=apne2, change=selfserve_cap=0.8, ttl=900s

jamie: nice. can we also nudge more capacity? any spare GPU headroom in nearby regions for cross-region fallback?

tiago: ap-south and us-west are both at ~70% utilization; no immediate spare pool that supports mistral-7b-instruct quant profile. Cross-region fallback would require model variant fallback (mistral-7b-8bit) which is available.

sasha: Proposal: 1) enforce self-serve soft throttle (done) 2) enable model-variant fallback for queued requests to mistral-7b-8bit with lower priority 3) notify growth-team to pause evals.

alex: agree. I'll open a quick guardrail to allow fallback for new requests only. old queued requests remain.

alex: command I ran to enable fallback:
```bash
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/fallbacks \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP" \
  -d '{"region":"apne2","model":"mistral-7b-instruct","fallback_to":"mistral-7b-8bit","policy":"new_requests_only","priority_penalty":1.4}'
```

deploy-bot: fallback policy registered (fb-8312).

kai: Also sanity-checking eviction policy: we should avoid evicting enterprise tokens. current logic honors priority_weights so we should be fine.

jamie: I'll DM growth-team lead to pause their evals for 30m. tagging @sasha for results.

sasha: on it. DM sent. they replied "pausing now, sorry for the noise" :thumbsup:

tiago: ops suggestion: start a one-off scale-up of 6 small GPU pods (if cloud quota allows) as temporary relief. cost will spike but buys time. Anyone want to approve?

alex: We have an uncommitted spare quota of 8 GPU slots in apne2 but they're in a different instance class and require a model kernel fallback test. Might take ~12-15m to boot and validate. Not ideal for immediate relief.

kai: Given fallback and throttle, I think we can avoid immediate scale-up. If queue doesn't drop below 1200 in 12m, we escalate and spin up pods.

jamie: Agreed. I'll keep watch on SLO alerts for p95/p99.

alex: Quick CE (customer experience) note: I flagged Acme's account in the incident tracker so CS is prepared if they see user impact.

sasha: Small follow-up: tweak policy to also cap embeddings per-second for redwood-embed-1 to 60rps for self-serve. doing that now.

deploy-bot: rate-limit update applied id=rl-4553 region=apne2 model=redwood-embed-1 limit=60rps

alex: queue depth 10m later: 1288, active_gpu_pods=44/48, avg_wait_ms=820. progress but still high.

tiago: good trend. keep throttles and fallback for another 15m. if we still have >1k queued we'll do scale-up and a short maintenance window to drain.

jamie: will record action items: 1) keep throttles/fallbacks 2) monitor for 15m 3) escalate to scale-up if needed 4) postmortem if growth eval not coordinated.

sasha: +1. I'll also add an alert rule to detect rapid single-tenant eval bursts and auto-label them so we can route to cost-control.

alex: thanks all. ping me if queue depth stops improving or if any enterprise reports latency regressions. :eyes:

kai: closing loop: last check at ts=1719866045 queue_depth_total=642, avg_wait_ms=220, p99=1.1s. letting throttles expire in 5m and will revert fallback if stable.

alex: solid. moving to resolved unless we see another spike.

sasha: resolved for now. documenting steps in runbook and adding a note to apne2 capacity slack channel.
